root.name: Benoni Defense: Classical Variation
root.moves: 1. d4 Nf6 2. c4 e6 3. Nf3 c5 4. d5 exd5 5. cxd5 d6 6. Nc3 g6 7. e4

overview: White has a broad centre with pawns on d5 and e4 and a space advantage; Black has a queenside pawn majority and the long diagonal, and plays ...Bg7, ...O-O and ...a6 with ...b5 or ...Re8 and ...Nbd7 against e4-e5. White aims for e5 or a kingside attack, Black for queenside play and a knight on e5 or c5. Imbalanced, tactical and theoretical, with strong counterplay for Black.

white_ideas.idea: Support e4-e5 with Bd3, Nd2 and O-O, or play h3 and Bf4 to prepare it.
Keep the space edge and the passed d-pawn potential.

black_ideas.idea: Break with ...b5 and ...a6 on the queenside and play on the open b- and e-files.
Pressure e4 with ...Nbd7, ...Re8 and a knight on e5 or c5.

typical_structures.structure: Modern Benoni: White d5/e4 centre against Black's queenside majority (a6, b5, c5, d6).

character.notes: Double-edged, with Black seeking counterplay and White's central break; any slip can lose quickly.

gambit.notes: No material is offered; pawn exchanges only.

structure.notes: Asymmetric central pawns with half-open e- and b-files for Black.

approach.notes: A recognised defence to 1.d4 played at the top.

level.notes: Heavy theory in the main lines and difficult plans.

sublines_that_differ.name: Modern Benoni via 3...c5 4.d5 e6
sublines_that_differ.moves: 1. d4 Nf6 2. c4 c5 3. d5 e6 4. Nc3 exd5 5. cxd5 d6 6. e4 g6 7. Nf3
sublines_that_differ.how: Same structure by transposition; the 3.Nf3 move order allows White more options.

character.reason: Unbalanced, double-edged, with real risk on both sides.

structure.reason: Asymmetric centre with half-open files; arguably closed.

plans.reason: Black plays on the queenside against White's central space.
